messages:
marta: quick sync idea: prototype a hybrid diurnal+tidal headroom for dedicated GPU pools. diurnal covers predictable hour-of-day baseline; tidal layer bumps short-term when correlated across tenants. aim: fewer cold starts but tightly bounded cost.
dennis: curious about operator impact. can this live on current AllocateLease/ReleaseLease surface?
keiko: yes if we encode hints in metadata. keep API unchanged: AllocateLease(tenant_id, slots, priority, annotations). annotations can include `headroom.type: diurnal|tidal|hybrid` and `headroom.hint: high|low`. controller decides actual prewarm.
owen: reclaimability is the big one. any prewarmed slot must be reclaimable within our P95 reclaim_latency (target 400ms). otherwise we break SLO. we should keep prewarms in preemptible tagset to speed eviction.
marta: agreed. operational controls: per-tenant daily_budget, per-shard global_budget, and a leaky-bucket rate limiter on headroom allocations so bursts can't overspend. If budget exceeded, degrade: switch tidal -> reactive and mark tenant with `headroom_throttled`.
dennis: telemetry wishlist: headroom_allocated_by_type, headroom_eviction_latency_p95, tidal_spike_frequency, diurnal_baseline_error (MAE), headroom_budget_used_pct. surface these in console and add alert when eviction_latency_p95 > 400ms or budget_used_pct > 90%.
keiko: policy nuance: tidal should be able to borrow from diurnal baseline if needed, but only if reclaimable=true on diurnal leases. otherwise treat diurnal as reserved. default diurnal leases are reclaimable but lower priority than explicit tenant active requests.
owen: test cases: replay past 90 days with hybrid on/off, synthetic tenant storm where tidal overshoots, and eviction stress where many tenants are reclaimed simultaneously. assert circuit-breaker trips and auto-disable headroom on shard.
marta: rollout plan: 1) dry-run telemetry for 2 weeks on one shard (no real allocations) 2) enable diurnal-only small budget (2-3% capacity) for 1 week 3) enable tidal augmentation under strict budget controls 4) monitor 2 weeks then expand. include kill-switch that immediately drains prewarms.
dennis: add CI regression: simulate overshoot and assert global_budget_flip to safe-mode. also include smoke that measures reclaim latency under eviction pressure.
infra-bot: pipeline queued for branch feature/hybrid-headroom. CI: unit tests pass, integration stub failing (known). :hammer_and_wrench:
marta: i'll author a short RFC with operator annotation examples, sample YAML for dashboard panels, and the staged rollout checklist. pinging @dennis @keiko for review. :raised_hands:
